key_big: Only about 10% of energy passes to the next level.

body_html:
How to think about it

An ecosystem is the living organisms of an area together with its non-living parts. Producers make food; consumers eat them; decomposers return nutrients to the soil. Each step in a food chain is a trophic level.

Only about 10% of the energy at one level reaches the next (the 10% law), so food chains are short. Harmful chemicals build up along a food chain (biological magnification). CFCs have thinned the ozone layer, which protects us from UV radiation. Biodegradable waste is broken down by decomposers; non-biodegradable waste stays for a long time.

Example

Producers hold 10,000 kJ. Energy for secondary consumers?

10,000 → 1,000 → 100

Answer: 100 kJ

Example

In grass → deer → lion, the deer is?

second level

Answer: a primary consumer

Common mistakes

  • Thinking energy is recycled in an ecosystem.
  • Counting trophic levels from the top.
  • Calling plastic biodegradable.
